title: Lamb youvetsi

ingredients.note: or the same amount of stock plus 1 tbsp balsamic for every 150ml

choose.title: Classic lamb shoulder (forgiving and rich)
steps: Prep: pat the shoulder dry and rub with the oil, spices and garlic. Place in a large deep roasting tin with the raw sliced onions, tomato purée, wine, chopped tomatoes, all the stock, cinnamon quill and bay leaves.
Roast: seal tightly with foil and bake at 160°C (140°C fan) for 2.5 to 3 hours until completely fall-apart tender.
Shred: uncover, pull the meat off the bone (skimming off any excess surface oil with a spoon), and discard the bone.

choose.title: Sous vide leg of lamb (best for flexible timing)
steps: Prep and cook, 13+ hours ahead: pat the leg dry, rub with the oil and spices, and bag with the smashed garlic (pad sharp bone ends with folded kitchen roll). Cook in a water bath at 74°C for 13–15 hours.

Make the sauce base: fry the sliced onions in the extra olive oil for 8–10 mins until soft. Mix in a large deep roasting tin with the tomato purée, wine, chopped tomatoes, the hot stock, keeping a little back to loosen the orzo later, cinnamon quill and bay leaves.

Hold or braise: shred the warm lamb off the bone straight into the roasting tin, pouring in all the hot bag juices. Seal tightly with foil and hold in the oven at 140–150°C (120–130°C fan) for 1.5–2.5 hours until you’re ready to finish.

choose.title: Slow-roasted leg of lamb (all-in-one oven method)
steps: Make the sauce base: mix the raw sliced onions in a large deep roasting tin with the tomato purée, wine, chopped tomatoes, all the stock, cinnamon quill and bay leaves.

Roast: pat the leg dry, rub with the oil, spices and garlic, and sit it directly in the sauce. Seal tightly with a double layer of foil. Bake at 160–170°C (140–150°C fan) for 2 to 2.5 hours until tender.
Shred: uncover, pull the lamb off the bone into bite-sized chunks with two forks, and discard the bone.
Ramp the heat: turn the oven up to 200°C (180°C fan) / gas mark 6. Fish out and discard the bay leaves and cinnamon quill from the hot lamb and sauce.
Add the orzo: stir the dry orzo straight into the bubbling broth so it is completely submerged. If the sauce looks thick rather than soupy, stir in a splash of hot water or stock.
Bake covered: re-cover the tin tightly with foil and bake for 15 minutes.
Uncover and brown: remove the foil, give the orzo a quick stir, and bake uncovered for 5 to 10 minutes until the pasta is tender and has absorbed the sauce.
Serve: scatter the crumbled feta and chopped parsley over the top, and bring straight to the table with the lemon wedges.
notes: Slow-braised Greek lamb and baked orzo. Serves 8–9.
